blocks.prompt: 15 [printed without its full stop] Prove that \(\tan^{-1} x + \cot^{-1}(x + 1) = \tan^{-1}(x^2 + x + 1)\).
blocks.explanation:
A sum of two inverse functions of different kinds, to be combined into one \(\tan^{-1}\).
Plan: change \(\cot^{-1}(x + 1)\) into \(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x + 1}\) (Example 4(iii)), add with formula (v), simplify. Then look at the values of \(x\) the first argument did not cover.
steps:
Given: \(\tan^{-1} x + \cot^{-1}(x + 1)\).
To prove: it equals \(\tan^{-1}(x^2 + x + 1)\).
Method: Two \(\tan^{-1}\) terms can be joined by formula (v), \(\tan^{-1} a + \tan^{-1} b = \tan^{-1}\frac{a + b}{1 - ab}\) (exact when \(ab < 1\)). So first write the \(\cot^{-1}\) as a \(\tan^{-1}\) with the book's Example 4(iii), \(\cot^{-1} u = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{u}\) (true for \(u > 0\)). We do \(x > -1\) first, then the remaining values.

Write \(\cot^{-1}\) as \(\tan^{-1}\) (for \(x > -1\))
\[\cot^{-1}(x + 1) = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{x + 1}\]
Why: Example 4(iii) with \(u = x + 1 > 0\).

Check that formula (v) may be used
\[x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x + 1} = \dfrac{x}{x + 1} < 1\]
Why: \(x < x + 1\); dividing by the positive number \(x + 1\) keeps the inequality. Formula (v) gives the sum exactly when the product of the two numbers is less than 1.

Add with formula (v)
\[\text{L.H.S} = \tan^{-1} x + \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{x + 1}\]
\[= \tan^{-1}\dfrac{x + \frac{1}{x + 1}}{1 - \frac{x}{x + 1}}\]
Why: Formula (v) with \(a = x\) and \(b = \frac{1}{x + 1}\).

Simplify the fraction
\[\text{top} = \dfrac{x(x + 1) + 1}{x + 1} = \dfrac{x^2 + x + 1}{x + 1}\]
\[\text{bottom} = \dfrac{(x + 1) - x}{x + 1} = \dfrac{1}{x + 1}\]
\[\dfrac{\text{top}}{\text{bottom}} = x^2 + x + 1\]
Why: Common denominators; dividing by \(\frac{1}{x + 1}\) cancels the \(x + 1\).

Conclude for \(x > -1\)
\[\text{L.H.S} = \tan^{-1}(x^2 + x + 1)\]
\[= \text{R.H.S}\]
Why: The fraction inside \(\tan^{-1}\) is exactly \(x^2 + x + 1\).

The other values of \(x\)
\[x = -1:\ \tan^{-1}(-1) + \cot^{-1} 0\]
\[= -\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \tan^{-1} 1\]
Why: At \(x = -1\), \(x^2 + x + 1 = 1\), so the identity holds. For \(x < -1\), \(\cot^{-1}(x + 1) = \pi + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x + 1}\) (the range of \(\cot^{-1}\) is \((0, \pi)\)), while the product \(\frac{x}{x + 1}\) is greater than 1 with both numbers negative, so \(\tan^{-1} x + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x + 1} = \tan^{-1}(x^2 + x + 1) - \pi\). The \(+\pi\) and \(-\pi\) cancel: the identity holds for every real \(x\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\tan^{-1} x + \cot^{-1}(x + 1) = \tan^{-1}(x^2 + x + 1)\) (true for every real \(x\)).
